packing: per shot c0..c(n-1), c0 = rightmost char; shots concatenated in returned order; MSB-first; partial byte dropped

prior.chosen: BEFORE the run: the most recent run (r2, both blocks); the r0/r1/r2 states are compared for Q1 only

K-R1.basis: of the two recalibrations seen (r0->r1, r1->r2) one left the state and one returned to it; the alternative outcome 'new state' is the refutation

K-R2.claim: the new state is stable within itself: r(C, D) >= 0.622

K-P1.claim: validated arm never worse than none: h_acc_val >= h_acc_none, out_val >= out_none, and coverage of D by the validated bound >= cov_min

K-P2.branch: r(prior, C) >= r_min (return to the r2 state)
claims: predicted_failing == excluded_C (both [72] on the dry runs)
K-P2.basis: dry run r2A->r2B gain 0.160103; r2AB->r0 gain 0.222106

scoring: K-P2 is scored only in the branch r(prior, C) >= r_min, K-P3 only in the other branch; the branch is a measurement, not a choice. If last_update changes between C and D, K-R2/K-P1 are UNMEASURED (reported, not re-scored).
interpretation: Q1 answers the physics (does the pattern return), Q2 answers the buyer (does a pre-chosen prior help, and does validation prevent the harm of a stale one). Statistics still cannot certify quantumness; receipts say 'statistical'.
